name: Cyprus
summary: Children are protected: they can claim up to a quarter of the estate, and a spouse or parent up to half where there are no children. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Cyprus has trusts and has been a Hague Trusts Convention state since 2017; foundations exist but their use for private family wealth is not clearly settled.
reserved_share: Per e-Justice: children can claim up to 25% of the net estate; with no children, a surviving spouse or parent can claim up to 50% (Wills and Succession Law, Cap. 195, art. 41, see also art. 51).
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: The 1985 Hague Trusts Convention entered into force for Cyprus on 1 June 2017 (ratified 15 March 2017). Domestic trusts exist under the Trustee Law (Cap. 193) and the International Trusts Law 69(I)/1992. Foundations are governed by the Associations and Foundations Law 104(I)/2017.
open_questions: e-Justice gives the reserved shares as 'up to' 25% and 50%; the exact mechanism (art. 41 Cap. 195) was not checked against the statute text.
Whether Law 104(I)/2017 allows purely private-benefit (family) foundations was not confirmed: only law-firm pages say foundations can serve succession planning.
